claims.text: In 2010, an estimated 184,000 deaths worldwide were attributable to sugar-sweetened beverage consumption.
In 2010, an estimated 133,000 deaths worldwide from diabetes mellitus were attributable to sugar-sweetened beverage consumption.
In 2010, an estimated 45,000 deaths worldwide from cardiovascular disease were attributable to sugar-sweetened beverage consumption.
In 2010, an estimated 6,450 deaths worldwide from cancers were attributable to sugar-sweetened beverage consumption.
Low-income countries accounted for 5.0% of global sugar-sweetened beverage-related deaths in 2010.
Middle-income countries accounted for 70.9% of global sugar-sweetened beverage-related deaths in 2010.
High-income countries accounted for 24.1% of global sugar-sweetened beverage-related deaths in 2010.
Proportional mortality attributable to sugar-sweetened beverages ranged from less than 1% in Japanese adults over 65 years to 30% in Mexican adults under 45 years.
Among the 20 most populous countries, Mexico had the highest absolute mortality attributable to sugar-sweetened beverages at 405 deaths per million adults.
Among the 20 most populous countries, Mexico had the highest proportional mortality attributable to sugar-sweetened beverages at 12.1%.
An estimated 8.5 million disability-adjusted life years worldwide were related to sugar-sweetened beverage intake in 2010.

evidence.description: Worldwide, the model estimated 184 000 (95% uncertainty interval, 161 000-208 000) deaths/y attributable to SSB consumption.
Model estimated 133 000 (126 000-139 000) deaths from diabetes mellitus attributable to SSB consumption.
Model estimated 45 000 (26 000-61 000) deaths from CVD attributable to SSB consumption.
Model estimated 6450 (4300-8600) deaths from cancers attributable to SSB consumption.
Five percent of SSB-related deaths occurred in low-income countries.
70.9% of SSB-related deaths occurred in middle-income countries.
24.1% of SSB-related deaths occurred in high-income countries.
Proportional mortality attributable to SSBs ranged from <1% in Japanese >65 years of age to 30% in Mexicans <45 years of age.
Among the 20 most populous countries, Mexico had largest absolute (405 deaths/million adults) deaths from SSBs.
Among the 20 most populous countries, Mexico had largest proportional (12.1%) deaths from SSBs.
A total of 8.5 (2.8, 19.2) million disability-adjusted life years were related to SSB intake (4.5% of diabetes mellitus-related disability-adjusted life years).

methodologies.name: Global Burden of Disease Population-Attributable Fraction Modeling
methodologies.description: Modeled cause-specific population-attributable fractions for sugar-sweetened beverage consumption combined with global dietary surveys, prospective cohort studies, and disease mortality/morbidity data across age, sex, and country strata.
datasets: Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors 2010 Study

limitations.text: The worldwide impact of SSBs on burdens of adiposity-related CVDs, cancers, and diabetes mellitus had not previously been assessed by nation, age, and sex.
